title: Tensor comparison for locally closed finite-free generators
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $R_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] for schemes $Y$ over $X$. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in ordinary unbounded derived categories of $R_Y$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], with relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ and $b:T\hookrightarrow X$ be constructible locally closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $L,M$ be $R_S$- and $R_T$-modules, respectively, each lisse [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], meaning finite free on a pro-etale cover. Form the scheme-theoretic fibre product $W=S\times_XT$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $r:W\to S$, $s:W\to T$ and immersion $c=ar=bs:W\hookrightarrow X$. For every locally closed immersion $h$, use the exact functor $h_!$ defined by closed direct image and open extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-weil-open-immersion], and exact inverse image $h^*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] with pulled-back coefficients. There is a natural isomorphism
$$ (a_!L)[0]\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_X}(b_!M)[0]\ \cong\ c_!\bigl((r^*L\otimes_{R_W}s^*M)[0]\bigr). $$
The right-hand tensor is underived; $r^*L\otimes_{R_W}s^*M$ is finite free on a common pro-etale cover, of rank $mn$ wherever the two factors have ranks $m,n$. In particular the displayed object has cohomology only in degree zero and its degree-zero cohomology is constructible with finite constant local models [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: it is this finite free module on $W$ and has zero model off $W$. The isomorphism uses the actual scheme fibre product, with its pulled-back coefficients, and is independent of choices of open/closed factorizations up to the normalized extension comparisons. Empty intersections and rank zero are allowed. No coefficient admissibility, finite-type or base-field hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proof (1), the two locally closed projection formulas and the base-change identification on S intersect T; used for the all-continuous lisse-generator calculation in AdmissibleTensorConstructibility, original paragraph 3.

proof.text: Choose closed-then-open factorizations of $a,b$. Base change of their closed and open factors shows that $r,s$ are locally closed immersions and, by composition of immersions (clause (e) of the permanence lemma), that their composites with $a,b$ are the same immersion $c:W\hookrightarrow X$. In particular this is the actual fibre product $S\times_XT$, rather than a chosen reduced intersection. Every intermediate open is Noetherian; every intermediate closed subscheme is Noetherian, since a closed immersion is finite type. Apply the same observation to the base-changed factors to see that $S,T,W$ are Noetherian. The underlying space of each has descending chains of closed subsets stabilizing; hence all its subsets are quasi-compact. Consequently the opens in these factorizations and all complementary opens are quasi-compact as morphisms (test on any affine open). All hypotheses of the open/closed projection formulas and the extension-coherence and base-change lemmas below therefore hold.

source.place: Proof (1), locally closed projection formulas and base change on the scheme fibre product

proof.text: The coefficient isomorphism $h^{-1}R_Z\cong R_Y$ holds for every morphism $h:Y\to Z$, for arbitrary condensed $\Lambda$, by the alpha-isomorphism lemma. Thus the inverse-image coefficient convention in extension coherence is the one in the statement. Pull back the trivializing pro-etale covers for $L,M$ to $W$ and refine them by their pairwise fibre products. On this common cover, exact monoidal inverse image identifies $r^*L$ with $R_W^m$ and $s^*M$ with $R_W^n$. Distributing the ordinary tensor over these finite sums gives the basis $e_i\otimes f_j$, indexed by $(i,j)$; the maps $e_i\otimes f_j\leftrightarrow e_{(i,j)}$ are mutually inverse. Hence $P=r^*L\otimes_{R_W}s^*M$ is lisse of rank $mn$ on this cover, including $m=0$ or $n=0$.

source.place: Proof (1), locally closed projection formulas and base change on the scheme fibre product

proof.text: Apply finite-free tensor exactness to $r^*L$ and $s^*M$. Each is flat as an internal $R_W$-module, with no restriction on $\Lambda$. The flat-single lemma makes their degree-zero complexes K-flat in the relative tensor convention. Computing derived tensor on these representatives therefore gives the natural comparison $r^*L[0]\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_W}s^*M[0]\cong P[0]$: its total complex has only the $(0,0)$ summand, so every differential is zero. This also fixes the underived identification used below.

source.place: Proof (1), locally closed projection formulas and base change on the scheme fibre product

proof.text:
For any of the locally closed immersions $h:D\hookrightarrow Z$ occurring here, factor $h=v i$ with $i:D\hookrightarrow V$ closed and $v:V\hookrightarrow Z$ open. The support projection formulas give, naturally in $A\in D(R_D)$ and $B\in D(R_Z)$,
$$ (v_!i_*A)\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\cong v_!\bigl(i_*A\otimes^{\mathbf L}v^*B\bigr)\cong v_!i_*\bigl(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}i^*v^*B\bigr). $$
Use the normalized extension comparison $h_!\cong v_!i_*$ and inverse-image composition to obtain $h_!A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\cong h_!(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}h^*B)$. These formulas apply to arbitrary unbounded inputs. Step 1 supplies the quasi-compact complementary opens; step 2 identifies supportPullback with the specified coefficient-compatible inverse image. The projection maps are the unit/counit-induced ones, so their restrictions to $D$ are the canonical tensor comparisons and restriction isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof (1), locally closed projection formulas and base change on the scheme fibre product

proof.text:
Factor $b=v\circ i$ with $i:T\hookrightarrow V$ closed and $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ open, let $k:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with image $X\setminus V$ and $u:V^\circ\hookrightarrow V$ the open complement of $i(T)$; both opens are quasi-compact and $X,V,S,S_V=S\times_XV$ are Noetherian, hence qcqs, by step 1. Base change of $v$ and $i$ along $a$ gives the open $v':S_V\hookrightarrow S$, the projection $a_V:S_V\to V$, the closed $i':W\hookrightarrow S_V$ with $r=v'i'$, and $s:W\to T$. Apply the base-change mates for the ring sheaf $R_X$ twice: $\alpha$ for the pair $(k,v)$ along $g=a$ gives $a^*v_!\cong v'_!a_V^*$, and $\beta$ for the pair $(i,u)$ along $g=a_V$ gives $a_V^*i_*\cong i'_*s^*$. The coefficient rings there are inverse images of $R_X$, identified with the pulled-back coefficients by step 2. With the normalized comparisons $b_!\cong v_!i_*$ and $r_!\cong v'_!i'_*$ this gives $a^*b_!M\cong r_!s^*M$. Its restriction along $r^*$ is the identity of $s^*M$ after the restriction isomorphisms and inverse-image composition comparisons: the adjoint of $\alpha^{-1}$ is $a_V^*$ of the open unit followed by the coefficient square comparison, so $v'^*\alpha$ is the canonical identification, and the adjoint of $\beta$ is the square comparison followed by $s^*$ of the closed counit, so $i'^*\beta$ is the canonical identification. All functors here are exact and applied to degree-zero objects, so this is also the corresponding derived identification. Apply step 4 first with $h=a$, then with $h=r$, using symmetry of tensor for the second application. The result is the chain
$$ a_!L[0]\otimes^{\mathbf L}b_!M[0]\cong a_!\bigl(L[0]\otimes^{\mathbf L}r_!s^*M[0]\bigr)\cong a_!r_!\bigl(r^*L[0]\otimes^{\mathbf L}s^*M[0]\bigr)\cong c_!P[0]. $$
The last arrow uses $\gamma_{a,r}:a_!r_!\cong c_!$ and step 3. This proves the displayed isomorphism by two projection calculations and one base-change input; it does not assume tensor constructibility.

source.place: Proof (1), locally closed projection formulas and base change on the scheme fibre product

proof.text: Each constituent of the chain in step 5 is natural in $L,M$. Changing open/closed factorizations and inserting the normalized extension comparisons gives a second map with the same source and target. The first isomorphism identifies that source with $c_!P[0]$, so their ratio is an endomorphism of $c_!P[0]$. After $c^*$, both maps are the ordinary tensor map on $r^*L,s^*M$: this follows from the unit/counit normalization of the projection maps, the identity normalization of the base-change isomorphism of step 5, and the identity normalization of $\gamma$. The tensor symmetries occur twice and cancel on $x\otimes y$. Hence this ratio restricts to the identity. The bijection on Hom sets induced by $c^*$ for two objects in the image of $c_!$ implies that the ratio is the identity. This proves independence of factorization in exactly the normalized sense asserted.

source.place: Proof (1), locally closed projection formulas and base change on the scheme fibre product

proof.text: Exactness of $c_!$ implies $\mathcal H^q(c_!P[0])=0$ for $q\ne0$ and $\mathcal H^0(c_!P[0])=c_!P$. Choose a closed-then-open factorization $c=v i$, with $v:V\hookrightarrow X$. Partition $X$ into the image of $W$, the open subset $V\setminus i(W)$, and the closed subset $X\setminus V$, giving the last one its reduced induced closed subscheme structure. These are disjoint locally closed strata; since $W$ is constructible by intersection of the two constructible immersion images, all three strata are constructible. Keep the given scheme $W$ as the first stratum. On it, $c^*c_!P=P$ by extension coherence. On the closed stratum $k':X\setminus V\hookrightarrow X$, the mate $\alpha$ for $v$ along $k'$ gives $k'^*v_!i_*P\cong v''_!(\cdots)$ with $v''$ the open immersion of the empty scheme $V\times_X(X\setminus V)$, hence zero. On the open stratum $u':V\setminus i(W)\hookrightarrow X$, factor $u'=vu_0$; then $u'^*c_!P\cong u_0^*v^*v_!i_*P\cong u_0^*i_*P$ by the restriction isomorphism, and the mate $\beta$ for $i$ along $u_0$ is extension from the empty fibre product, hence zero. By step 2, on the first stratum $P$ has the finite constant scalar model $R^{mn}=R\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}\Lambda(*)^{mn}$, and elsewhere the model is zero. This finite stratification verifies the constructibility definition for every condensed $\Lambda$. If $W$ is empty, all these restrictions are zero; the same formulas cover zero ranks and the zero ring.
